description: This data set gives, hour by hour, how many nurses were working on four wards of University Hospital Augsburg in Germany and how many were absent, whether planned or unexpectedly. The producers are Emily Schiller, Simon Mueller and Jan-Philipp Steghoefer of the software company XITASO, with Kathrin Ebertsch of the hospital, who released it for research on staff scheduling. Coverage is eighteen months, from 1 January 2022 to 30 June 2023, a period that includes late waves of COVID-19, across four wards in different medical areas. Each row has the total nursing staff deployed and the number of planned and unplanned absences. The CSV file is available as a free download from Zenodo under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence. Caveats: four wards of one hospital, no patient numbers or acuity to relate staffing to demand, and ward identities are generalised. Simulation uses: forecasting unplanned staff absence, which often limits hospital capacity more than beds do during epidemics or heatwaves, and testing rostering and float pool policies. Related records: the perinatal and bed data sets such as the Italian hospital beds (data-italy-hospital-beds-by-structure-2010-2017) cover physical capacity, and patientflow (model-patientflow) forecasts bed demand.
